audit.why: Mel at 1 and again at 6, Akali from 3 and from first item, matches both on-disk charts. 54.27% over 15 games is far too small a sample to move a chart on, so nothing was touched - the mirror entry mel__akali.json reaches the same conclusion about the sample.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 row was generic template text and breakdown.spikes named 'Solar Snare online, level 6, first item' with no numbers. Mel's real spike ability never appeared.
audit.why: Golden Eclipse is her level-6 spike: 120/100/80s, effectively global at 25000 range, and it strikes everything carrying Overwhelm stacks. Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s - the longest and most punishable cooldown in the lane, and far more important to track than Solar Snare's 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, breakdown.spikes, breakdown.cooldowns, winCon and report[9].t rebuilt on the 38s Rebuttal and the 120s global Golden Eclipse.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mel's ability slots are wrong across the content layer: spikes[0].text says 'her ranged Q (Solar Snare) and W (Radiant Volley)' - both swapped - and whys[0] repeats 'her Q snare and W poke'. Worse, Rebuttal is called her R three times ('her R, Rebuttal, reflects projectiles', 'a reflect ult'), when Rebuttal is her W and her actual ultimate, Golden Eclipse, is named nowhere in either layer.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Q Radiant Volley (950 poke zone), W Rebuttal (barrier that reflects projectiles and prevents her damage, 38/35/33/29/26s), E Solar Snare (1000-range root), R Golden Eclipse (25000 range, hits everything holding Overwhelm). A player told to 'wait out her R reflect' will hold their combo for a 120s ultimate that does not reflect anything, and will walk into the 38s barrier that does. The reflect also matters specifically because Five Point Strike and Shuriken Flip are Akali's two projectile abilities - they come back at her - while Perfect Execution is a dash whose damage is merely prevented.

edits.before: This is where I flip it. With W-Shroud I drop a cloud on her Q line, go untargetable and invisible, and walk my Assassin's Mark ring onto her — the empowered auto plus a max-range Q slow out-trades her poke, and she has no dash to escape me. At 6 my R is the kill: E-Flip to stick onto her, but respect her R — Rebuttal reflects and blocks, so I bait or wait out that window, then first-cast R through her and second-cast R to execute her low. One clean combo deletes an immobile mage.

edits.before: My level-6-to-first-item spike is when I have to close this. With Lich Bane or Rocketbelt I one-shot her on every E-Flip engage, and Shroud makes her skillshots whiff. But she's a scaling AP mage with a reflect ult and two items of zone control — if the game drags, her poke and Rebuttal punish my all-in pattern and I run out of windows. Win it before she stacks items; don't let a 54% lane rot into a 50-minute poke war I can't burst through.

notes: The slot errors here were systemic, not a typo: Mel's Q and E were swapped in the content layer and her W (Rebuttal) was called her ultimate three times, while her real ultimate (Golden Eclipse) appeared nowhere in either layer. Worth checking whether the same Mel entry template was used for other champions. I did not touch the repeated claim that Twilight Shroud's untargetability blanks Solar Snare's root or a Golden Eclipse detonation — that is not answerable from Riot's ability text and the mirror entry flagged the same thing as unverified.
